---
title: "Genitive Metaphors in the Kitáb-i-Íqán"
subtitle: "Part One · Paragraphs 1–101"
toc: true
toc-depth: 2
page-layout: full
---

::: {.lead .lead-sm}
A **genitive metaphor** is a metaphor built out of a possessive or descriptive construction — 'a flood of messages'. One noun is the actual subject (messages), the other is a figurative image (flood). In English the two are almost always joined by the word *of*.

Bahá'u'lláh uses the construction constantly, and He uses it to interpret: He names an image and the reality it stands for in the same breath — the **ocean** of *true understanding*, the **earth** of *divine knowledge*, the **heaven** of *divine Revelation*.

This page gathers every such pair in the first part of the Book of Certitude — 122 images, 300 phrases, 327 occurrences. They are listed alphabetically by image, and under each image the phrases appear in the order they first occur. The numbers are paragraph numbers.
:::
